insights.insight: Cumulative verified spend on the Crinkl protocol crossed $2M on June 14 and reached $2.05M by June 16 — deterministic purchase confirmation at a scale that begins to support statistically meaningful targeting segments across grocery, dining, and retail.

The protocol is adding roughly 410 verified receipts per day on a sustained basis, producing ~10,700 receipts over the last 26 days — a volume floor that gives campaign planners a predictable signal refresh rate rather than a one-time data snapshot.

insights.topic: Basket compression: grocery and convenience dominating mix
insights.insight: The 7-day average basket has compressed from ~$80 to ~$57 as grocery and gas-convenience receipts make up an increasing share of volume; brands in higher-consideration categories should note that GMV growth currently requires proportionally more receipt volume to sustain, which affects segment density for big-ticket verticals.

A distinct bucket of 189 receipts in the 14-day window carries an average basket of ~$364 — roughly 6x the grocery average — with category attribution still unresolved; if this resolves to large-ticket retail, electronics, or B2B spend, it represents a high-value targeting segment currently invisible to category-level buyers.

insights.topic: Brand footprint broadening beyond grocery core
insights.insight: Target (116 receipts) and Publix entered the top-brand threshold in the current 14-day window alongside Walmart, Costco, and Kroger — signaling that the verified purchase graph is expanding from a warehouse/grocery core into mainstream mass-market retail, widening the addressable audience for CPG and general merchandise brands.

insights.topic: Geographic coverage at new high: 18 metros
insights.insight: The protocol now shows verified purchase signals across 18 metro areas, a new high, though coverage remains pulse-based rather than continuous — marketers planning geo-targeted activations should treat current metro breadth as directional and validate specific CBSA depth before committing spend.
